clue.text: Exceptional Latin hero of great courage

definitions.note: the clue phrase describes a brave person; the solution is the noun for such a person, a byname of Richard I

indicators.note: exceptional suggests something out of the ordinary, so these letters leave their usual order

explanation.surface: A Roman warrior singled out for outstanding bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exceptional' rearranges LATIN HERO. The definition is adjectival in form, but the solution names someone with that quality.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with the heart of a lion is proverbially brave, the nickname given to Richard I of England.

clue.text: Fail to mention that time off work is not on

parts.note: leave is authorised absence from a job
a light that is not on is out

explanation.surface: Someone forgets to report that an employee's holiday has been cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something from an account is to skip it, failing to mention it.

clue.text: Let battle commence in a hot spot

definitions.meaning: to begin shooting at the enemy
an uncovered hearth fire is literally a hot place

explanation.surface: A general gives the order to start the fight from a dangerous position.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordering troops to start shooting begins a battle; a grate burning without a screen is also a hot spot in the room.

clue.text: Vacuum left by former FBI chief

definitions.meaning: to clean a carpet with a suction cleaner
J Edgar ... ran the Bureau for nearly fifty years

explanation.surface: A gap in leadership is left when a famous FBI director departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left by' is a link joining the two definitions; HOOVER is the British brand name used as a verb for vacuum cleaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The brand of vacuum cleaner gives the British verb for cleaning with one, and J Edgar of that surname led the FBI.

clue.text: Suit I found in Ealing area

indicators.note: a thing found in a place is located inside it, so one letter sits within the district

parts.note: Acton is a district in the London borough of Ealing

explanation.surface: A lawsuit is turned up in a west London district.
explanation.walkthrough: ACTON is a district of west London, in the borough of Ealing.
explanation.definitionFit: A suit at law is a legal proceeding, also called an action in court.

clue.text: Prepares to play golf with team in the North-East

definitions.note: the clue phrase locates a place; the solution is a place in that region

parts.note: a golfer tees, or tees up, the ball before driving
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A golfer gets ready for a round with friends in northern England.
explanation.walkthrough: TEESSIDE is the industrial area around the River Tees in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: This conurbation around Middlesbrough lies in England's North-East region.

clue.text: A huge number retired in India

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a mass is a great quantity

explanation.surface: A great many people went into retirement in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' signals the reversal. The definition 'in India' is a place inside the country: Assam is an Indian state.
explanation.definitionFit: This north-eastern state is part of India, famous for its tea gardens.

clue.text: Weapon in dry sack

parts.note: to air laundry is to dry it out
to rifle or sack a place is to plunder it

explanation.surface: A gun is hidden inside a sherry-style bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' and 'sack' look like a wine (sack is old sherry), but both are verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun firing pellets by compressed gas is a light weapon.

clue.text: One held by Spanish man of high rank

indicators.note: something held by another is enclosed within it, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: senor is Spanish for a gentleman
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A Spanish gentleman of high standing has someone in his grip.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone superior in rank or status is described as senior to others.

clue.text: Manage somehow to produce and act

parts.note: to make is to produce
to do is to act

explanation.surface: Someone directs a stage production and has to perform in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To get by with whatever is available is to cope, managing somehow.

clue.text: Herb discovers the price of beer

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
a cost is a price

explanation.surface: A gardener finds out how much a pint costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'price of beer' gives ALE COST in that order: the beer first, then its price.
explanation.definitionFit: Costmary, a plant once used to flavour ale, is an aromatic herb.

clue.text: Available for use at church

explanation.surface: Something is ready for use during worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipment that is operational is ready to use, and a worshipper attending a church ceremony is also present at one.

clue.text: Old PC North nis a character

parts.note: a micro is a microcomputer, a personal computer

explanation.surface: An old police officer from the north is quite a figure.
explanation.walkthrough: PC suggests a police constable but is a personal computer; 'character' means a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifteenth letter of the Greek alphabet is a written character.

clue.text: Hell-fire

definitions.meaning: the place of damnation, as in Dante's poem

explanation.surface: A preacher warns of fire and brimstone.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante's poem names the underworld of torment, and the word also means a raging blaze.

clue.text: Deplore the trend set by James Stuart

indicators.note: set in the sense of arranged or put in place, so these letters are placed in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone laments a fashion started by a royal exile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' rearranges DEPLORE THE TREND. James Francis Edward Stuart, son of James II, claimed the British throne from exile.
explanation.definitionFit: James Francis Edward Stuart, exiled son of James II, claimed the British crown and was nicknamed so by his enemies.

clue.text: Attack a lazy loafer

definitions.meaning: to set upon someone, beat them
an idle person who avoids work

explanation.surface: Someone sets upon an idle good-for-nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay about someone is to hit out vigorously, and the joined noun names an idler who avoids work.

clue.text: Writer suing odd underwater swimmers

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of order, so the letters of suing are rearranged

explanation.surface: An author takes some eccentric divers to court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' is the anagram signal; 'underwater swimmers' suggests divers, but these are birds.
explanation.definitionFit: These flightless Antarctic birds swim fast beneath the sea, using their wings as flippers.

clue.text: Daimonic disruption in the West Indies

definitions.note: the clue phrase locates a place; the solution is an island there

indicators.note: disruption throws things out of order, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Demonic upheaval breaks out in the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: This island republic lies in the Lesser Antilles of the Caribbean.

clue.text: Staunch Labour supporter is not from Oxbridge

definitions.note: describes a university outside the ancient pair

parts.note: red is the colour of the left, so a socialist is a red
a brick is a staunch, reliable friend

explanation.surface: A loyal socialist voter did not go to an elite university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brick' as a dependable person is old British slang; redbrick universities are the Victorian civic ones, as opposed to Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: British civic universities founded around 1900 were built of brick, contrasted with the old stone colleges.

clue.text: Persevere despite commotion

explanation.surface: Someone keeps going in spite of all the fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going is to continue, and a fuss or palaver is the hyphenated noun.

clue.text: Merry monarch grasped divine way to cook eggs

definitions.note: a noun phrase for a cooking method; the solution is the verb naming it

indicators.note: a thing grasped is held inside, so the second piece goes within the first

parts.note: Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme was a merry old soul
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a clergyman, a divine

explanation.surface: Charles II held a clergyman's view on how eggs should be done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merry monarch' points to Charles II, but here it is Old King Cole, the merry old soul of the nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs can be cooked gently in water just below boiling, a method also meaning to pamper.

clue.text: Council tax earns stern, reproof

definitions.meaning: the old local property tax, the rates

explanation.surface: A local levy draws a harsh rebuke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earns' is a link. Rates were the British local property tax before council tax; a rating is also an old word for a scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: Assessing property for rates was the old basis of British local taxation, and the word also means a severe scolding.

clue.text: Dismayed when a sovereign prepared for war

parts.note: a sovereign is a pound coin, abbreviated L
an army that is armed is ready to fight

explanation.surface: Panic spreads when a king mobilises his army.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign was a British gold pound coin, and L is the abbreviation for pound.
explanation.definitionFit: To be filled with sudden fear or anxiety is to be frightened and dismayed.

clue.text: Ideal arrangement by key Roman magistrate

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things in order, so the letters of the word are reordered

parts.note: E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A neat musical setting is prepared for an official of ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' sounds musical beside 'key', but it is the anagram signal; 'key' gives a note name.
explanation.definitionFit: This official in ancient Rome oversaw public buildings, games and the corn supply.

clue.text: Man is by nature a political (Aristotle)

definitions.text: Man is by nature a political (Aristotle)

parts.words: Man is by nature a political (Aristotle)
parts.note: a famous quotation from the Politics with its final word missing; the solver completes it

explanation.surface: A line from Greek philosophy about human nature, left unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle's Politics calls humans creatures naturally suited to living in a city-state.

clue.text: Obliged to produce tax before spring

indicators.note: one word coming before another means it is placed first

parts.note: a duty is a tax on goods
a bound is a leap or spring

explanation.surface: Someone is forced to pay a levy before the season turns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' suggests the season but is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bound by a moral responsibility means being compelled or obliged to act.

clue.text: Is post given to one of the Aga Khan's subjects?

definitions.note: the clue phrase is plural; the solution names one member of that sect

parts.note: mail is the post
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A question whether letters are sent to a follower of the Aga Khan.
explanation.walkthrough: The Aga Khan is the leader of the Ismaili branch of Shia Islam.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of this Shia Muslim sect regard the Aga Khan as their imam.

clue.text: Crew from a freighter

indicators.note: from signals letters taken out of the following words, the run sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Sailors are taken off a cargo ship.
explanation.walkthrough: A rowing crew of eight oarsmen is called an eight.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing boat with eight oarsmen, and its team, is named for the number of rowers.

clue.text: Woman will support and old sailor

parts.note: she is a pronoun for a woman
'll is the contracted form of will
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: A wife promises to stand by a veteran seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: A shellback is a sailor who has crossed the equator, hence a seasoned old hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A seasoned seaman, especially one who has crossed the equator, is nicknamed thus.
